title: Ad-hoc function invocation triage - session breadcrumbs
content:
High-level: quick self-note log from a messy triage session investigating recurring partial/invalid function-call JSON from the hosted API (seen in customer telemetry). Goal: capture commands run, observed bytes, reproducible minimal inputs, and hypotheses to pass to the runtime team.

Summary of symptom:
- Customer (customer-a) sees repeated ‘malformed JSON’ in tool-call payloads from model X when using streaming=true + function_call=auto. Errors occur ~1:200 requests; spikes align with messages that include long code blocks or lots of nested lists.
- Decoder output occasionally truncates inside a JSON value (e.g., truncated string or trailing comma present), causing downstream JSON.parse to fail.
- Non-streaming requests do not reproduce. Intermittent and hard to repro locally.

Session timeline / breadcrumbs:
1) 2025-11-02 10:12 — pulled sample event from prod logs: payload_id=evt-20251102-81, user_id=redacted. Raw chunks (base64) attached below. Observed last chunk ends with '"notes": "This is a long description that ends mid-sent' (cut).
2) 10:30 — ran local streaming client (node) with identical prompt and streaming chunk size set to 1024 bytes. No repro.
3) 11:00 — decreased chunk size (512 -> 128) and added artificial network jitter (tc qdisc) — still no repro.
4) 12:25 — tried using python aiohttp streaming harness (closer to prod agent in request pattern). One partial failure after ~400 iterations. Grabbed raw tcpdump.
5) 13:05 — isolated minimal prompt that triggered it in python harness (see repro_minimal_prompt below).
6) 13:40 — hypothesis: chunk boundary aligns with open JSON string and our streaming boundary trimming/concatenation logic drops or corrupts last bytes under specific UTF-8 multi-byte char alignment.
7) 14:10 — tested with deliberately injected multi-byte unicode (emoji and CJK) in prompts — reproduced reliably when chunk boundary bisected a multi-byte char.

Commands tried (selected):
- node reproduce_stream.js --prompt-file sample.txt --chunk-size=1024 --streaming=true
- tc qdisc add dev lo root netem delay 20ms loss 0.1%
- python -m scripts.stream_invoke --prompt=... --n=1000 --chunk=128 --user-agent="triage-harness"
- tcpdump -s 0 -w /tmp/prod-capture.pcap host 10.0.4.12 and port 443
- openssl s_client -quiet -connect api.redwood.example.com:443 < /tmp/req.bin > /tmp/res.bin

Key artifacts captured:
- raw_chunks_evt-20251102-81.txt (hex of received chunks) — last chunk partial string
- pcap_partial_corrupt.pcap — shows TLS records that split at 3rd byte of a 4-byte UTF-8 emoji (U+1F4A9)
- repro_harness.py — stripped down python async stream runner (see snippet below)

Minimal repro prompt (repro_minimal_prompt):
"Please emit a tool call as JSON only.
Tool: report_issue
Args: {
  \"summary\": \"Unicode boundary test\",
  \"notes\": \"Long text with emoji: 💩💩💩 and extra filler to push length beyond chunk boundary\"
}
"

Observed error snippets (copied from client logs):
- JSONDecodeError: Expecting ',' delimiter: line 1 column 243 (char 242)
- Received partial JSON: '{"name":"report_issue","args":{"summary":"Unicode boundary test","notes":"Long text with emoji: \xf0\x9f\x92' 
- Runtime concatenation warning (internal): "last_chunk_missing_end_byte" for connection conn-4472

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Streaming reassembly bug in client library (my earlier suspicion). But repro in multiple clients (node + python), so less likely.
2) TLS record boundary + UTF-8 multi-byte char splitting combined with our streaming frame concat logic that assumes boundaries align with UTF-8 characters. If server code uses byte-level slicing and converts to string without verifying full codepoint, splits can produce invalid UTF-8 sequences which, depending on language, may be dropped or replaced with U+FFFD causing malformed JSON.
3) Server runtime attempts to 'repair' invalid UTF-8 by dropping bytes, resulting in truncated JSON values and trailing commas.
4) Model output itself includes invalid escapes or control chars occasionally when near length limit.

Experiments to validate hypothesis 2/3 (notes & results):
- Injected multibyte chars exactly at known chunk boundaries in harness -> reproduce rate jumped to ~1:4 (was 1:200). Good signal.
- Decoded raw TLS payload -> confirmed TLS record split across multi-byte char (pcap).
- Modified client to delay assembly until all TLS records for message done (simulate stricter join) -> repro rate dropped to 0/600. Suggests concatenation/join timing matters.
- Server-side attempted quick patch (log-only) to detect invalid UTF-8 sequences at reassembly and log connection id when seen. New logs show same conn-4472 flagged repeatedly.

Immediate mitigations suggested (short-term):
- For customers hit by this: advise disabling streaming or using smaller unicode-free prompts as workaround (customer-facing note).
- Push server-side defensive check: when reassembling streaming bytes, validate UTF-8 boundaries and buffer incomplete codepoints until next chunk before decoding to string. Fallback: treat as binary and reconstruct cautiously.
- Instrument runtime to emit metric: count_invalid_utf8_reassemblies per connection/route.

Longer term / engineering asks:
- Runtime: ensure reassembly code handles arbitrary byte splits; do not assume chunk boundaries align to codepoint boundaries. Add unit tests that simulate partial multibyte splits.
- SDK: add optional safe_stream_mode that will always reassemble bytes as binary and validate UTF-8 before turning into text events (opt-in if customer needs strict correctness).
- Product: consider educating customers in docs about streaming caveats with UTF-8 heavy payloads and recommend the safe config.

Repro harness snippet (repro_harness.py):
```python
# trimmed for doc
async def stream_invoke(prompt, chunk_size):
    async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as s:
        async with s.post(url, json={"prompt": prompt, "stream": True}) as r:
            async for raw_chunk in r.content.iter_chunked(chunk_size):
                # yield raw bytes to consumer
                yield raw_chunk
```
Note: iter_chunked returns bytes; we were doing chunk.decode('utf-8', errors='replace') directly which hides split boundary issues.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Is there any codepath in the runtime that does additional normalization (NFKC/NFD) on output before framing? That could interact with byte-level splits.
- Are there intermediary proxies/load-balancers that might re-chunk TLS records? Need infra to confirm LB behavior.
- Should we auto-detect suspicious partial UTF-8 on the client and request a re-send or fallback to non-streaming? UX tradeoffs to discuss.

Next steps (assignments):
- @Ethan: add unit tests to runtime reassembly module simulating TLS-level splits for multibyte chars (INF-2137).
- @Lina: coordinate with infra to verify LB/TLS behavior in front of the runtime (who owns that path?).
- @Maya (me): draft customer advisory and quick SDK patch for safe_stream_mode prototype.

Notes to self: keep raw_chunks_evt-20251102-81.txt and pcap in my temp dir until PR merges. If this turns out to be client bug, we'll still need runtime telemetry to pinpoint broken connections (we can't trust client-side logs alone).

End of scratchpad.
